method: Manual content audit of lesson tutorials/examples/canonical and representative practice across skill groups, full bank captured. Whole-lesson decisions; graph used only to discover dependencies. Retained direct/indirect prerequisites checked by actual question demand. No match-ma-lesson, assignment edits or learner changes.

decisions.topic_name: Gaussian Elimination For NxM Systems of Equations
decisions.reason: The rectangular/free-variable extension is short enough to earn its place before null-space and 4x6 homework work. Studied RREF/singular 3x3 supply operations, but no direct learned rectangular lesson exists.

evidence.detail: 2 equations/3 unknowns reduced to x=1-4z,y=-3z and affine vector form.
Rectangular consistent system: reduce and give its general solution.

decisions.downstream_benefit: Ease Null Space, null-basis and WHW-5 4x6 rank work; explicit free versus pivot variables.

decisions.topic_name: Subspaces of N-Dimensional Space
decisions.reason: First actual subspace criterion lesson; symbolic arbitrary-vector closure examples have real instructional value before image proofs. Entire practice is line/plane classification, so proof production remains a separate transfer demand.

evidence.detail: Proves y=3x closed using arbitrary u,v,c; explains zero necessity.
Builds line through origin from two points, proves closure componentwise.
Proves z=4x-2y closed by symbolic addition and scaling.
Select zero membership/addition/scalar closure/subspace for x=2y.

decisions.downstream_benefit: Guide 2 Subspace Test; guide 3 scalar-closure disproof; WHW-5 dot-product and parametric-set subspace claims.

decisions.topic_name: Subspaces of N-Dimensional Space: Geometric Interpretation
decisions.reason: Outside expansion, but earns a place as a concrete sequel: bounded and nonlinear sets containing zero defeat the misleading origin-only heuristic from line/plane examples.

evidence.detail: Explains failure of addition/scaling on non-subspace diagrams.
x^2=y fails scaling; shifted parametric line requires testing origin.
Disk radius 1 fails sufficiently large scaling; half-plane fails negation.
Distinguishes homogeneous plane, affine set, and trivial zero set defined by sum of squares <=0.

decisions.downstream_benefit: Guide 3 bounded slab |u1|<=4; basis/null/column lessons use zero/line/plane interpretation.

decisions.topic_name: The Column Space of a Matrix
decisions.reason: Keep the concrete membership/consistency foundation even though Image/Rank repeats the definition later. Learner has no learned column-space lesson; this stages a new set concept before basis extraction/rank/image vocabulary.

evidence.detail: Defines column space as span and converts membership to Ax=b.
Finds k for consistency with a 3x2 coefficient matrix.
Col(A) is a subspace of R^m for m x n A; membership iff consistency.
Solve membership then coefficient product.

decisions.downstream_benefit: Image witness idea and WHW-5 column-space/rank interpretation; separates output space R^m from input space R^n.

decisions.topic_name: The Null Space of a Matrix
decisions.reason: Keep elementary zero-product membership and parametric null-set work before extracting a basis. Matrix-vector product is mastered; the null-set interpretation is unstudied and has only one recorded practice mass.

evidence.detail: Checks three candidates by computing A b_i.
Null(A)={(-3x2,x2):x2 real}; distinguishes free/basic variable.
Invertible 2x2 example yields Null(A)={0}.
Find k so vector belongs to Null(A).

decisions.downstream_benefit: Null-basis/nullity/IMT chain; WHW-5 dependence via nonzero homogeneous solution.

decisions.topic_name: Finding a Basis of a Span
decisions.reason: Foundational basis lesson is needed despite learned independence: distinguishes independent spanning subset from redundant generating set and explains why deletion preserves span.

evidence.detail: Substitutes a3=-a1+3a2 into an arbitrary original linear combination to prove unchanged span.
Find basis via pivots, explicitly original columns.
Check proposed basis and express fourth vector using three coefficients.
Both independence and same-span reasoning, then coefficients.

decisions.downstream_benefit: WHW-4 dependence relations/independent same-span sets; WHW-5 basis/dimension; generic basis expansion in guide 4.

decisions.topic_name: Expressing the Coordinates of a Vector in a Given Basis
decisions.reason: Coordinates for an arbitrary ordered basis are not supplied by mastered standard-matrix computation. Concrete forward/reverse representation practice substantially eases applying T to an expansion in an arbitrary basis.

evidence.detail: Defines basis coordinates as unique coefficients; 2D subspace of R3 example.
Solves coordinates in a three-vector nonstandard basis.
Shows standard basis independence, spanning, and equality of standard coordinates and components.
Permuted standard vectors make order matter.

decisions.downstream_benefit: Guide 4 im(T)=span(T(v_i)); matrix in basis/standard basis course coverage.

decisions.topic_name: Finding a Basis of the Column Space of a Matrix
decisions.reason: Although Basis of a Span has the algorithm, retain matrix-specific practice and original-column warning: WHW-5 #8 requires the column-space basis alongside a different row-basis rule. No mastered basis-extraction topic supplies this distinction.

evidence.detail: Col(A) basis from original pivot columns, not echelon columns.
Nonpivot RREF entries supply a redundant original column combination.
3x4 matrix, check proposed column basis and recover fourth-column coefficients.
3x3 matrix has rank 2; retain original columns 1,2.

decisions.downstream_benefit: WHW-5 bases for spans and column space; prepares dimension/rank with concrete objects.

decisions.topic_name: The Dimension of a Span
decisions.reason: Basis size as dimension is new; includes ambient dim(R^n)=n needed for cardinality proofs, not merely numerical rank.

evidence.detail: Every basis has the same number of vectors; defines dimension.
Row reduction finds dimension 1 of redundant 3-vector span.
Standard basis has n vectors, dim(R^n)=n.
Compute dimension by row reduction.

decisions.downstream_benefit: WHW-5 basis/dimension and too-many-vectors arguments; rank definition.

decisions.topic_name: The Rank of a Matrix
decisions.reason: Links dimension/column basis to pivots and nonzero echelon rows. No learned rank record exists, so do not replace conceptual rank learning with mastered pivot counting.

evidence.detail: Defines rank=dim Col(A) and explains two original columns form basis.
4x7 matrix with 3 nonpivots has rank 4.
Rank equals pivot count and nonzero echelon-row count.
Reduce 4x4 matrix and find rank.

decisions.downstream_benefit: WHW-5 final 4x6 rank task, ambient dimension bounds, image rank and nullity.

decisions.topic_name: Finding a Basis of the Null Space of a Matrix
decisions.reason: Outside expansion and necessary for efficient whole-lesson nullity/IMT learning: turns free-variable descriptions into independent generators, including empty basis of zero space.

evidence.detail: Derives a null basis and explicitly states basis of {0} is empty set.
Two free parameters in R4 split into two generators.
Rectangular RREF with pivots 1,3 gives free coordinates 2,4.
3x4 RREF yields a one-vector null basis.

decisions.downstream_benefit: Dimension of Null Space introductory derivation and IMT practice about empty basis; kernel basis practice if retained.

decisions.topic_name: The Dimension of the Null Space of a Matrix
decisions.reason: Outside expansion but supplies the genuinely new correspondence free variables <-> null basis size before IMT asks students to interpret parametric null spaces.

evidence.detail: One nonpivot gives explicit one-vector basis and dimension 1.
9x11 with 9 pivots has null dimension 2.
4x4 row reduction yields nullity 1.
4x5 null dimension from reduction.

decisions.downstream_benefit: IMT full rank/nullity-zero equivalence; WHW-5 too-many-columns nontrivial homogeneous solution.

decisions.topic_name: The Invertible Matrix Theorem in Terms of 2x2 Systems of Equations
decisions.reason: Keep a concrete first statement of inverse/determinant/unique-solution equivalence before its higher-dimensional vector-space reformulation. Entire questions are theorem implications, so inverse-matrix solving lesson is not required beforehand.

evidence.detail: Equivalent invertibility, unique Ax=b for all b, unique homogeneous zero, one line intersection, nonzero determinant.
Parameterized 2x2 determinant used to infer system properties.
Given two lines intersect once, complete implication.

decisions.downstream_benefit: General dimension/rank/nullity IMT and determinant implications from homework.

decisions.topic_name: The Invertible Matrix Theorem in Terms of Dimension, Rank and Nullity
decisions.reason: New finite-dimensional equivalences explicitly explain why nullity zero forces all columns pivotal and Col(A)=R^n. This eases WHW-5 independent n vectors -> full span rather than leaving a theorem-transfer leap.

evidence.detail: Explains invertible -> Null={0} -> nullity0 -> all columns pivot -> rank n -> Col=R^n.
Parametric 1D null space of 4x4 gives noninvertibility/rank not 4.
Nonzero determinant implies empty null-space basis and n pivot columns.

decisions.downstream_benefit: WHW-5 independent five vectors in R5 span; rank/nullity section coverage; integrates determinant and vector-space views.

decisions.topic_name: The Rank-Nullity Theorem
decisions.reason: Outside expansion, compact and explicitly covers matrix rank-nullity (confirmed textbook 4.10.5); rank and nullity separately do not themselves give the integrated theorem practice.

evidence.detail: Pivot+nonpivot columns=n yields rank+nullity=n for nonsquare matrices.
3x5 matrix with 3-element column basis has null dimension 2.
Infer rank from a two-parameter null space in R4.
Combine IMT with rank-nullity and a given null-space span.

decisions.downstream_benefit: Rectangular rank/nullity inference; WHW-5 dimension bounds; whole course section explicitly named.

decisions.topic_name: The Image and Rank of a Linear Transformation
decisions.reason: Actual image membership, standard-matrix bridge and rank(T)=dim im(T) need a complete lesson. It does not prove image closure or the arbitrary-basis image equality.

evidence.detail: Defines image by existence of preimage and gives concrete witness.
im(T)=Col(T)=span of standard-matrix columns.
Find a preimage by solving Tx=b.
Compute transformation rank from matrix.

decisions.downstream_benefit: Guide 2 image witness interpretation; guide 4 standard-basis special case; chapter5 image/rank.

decisions.topic_name: The Kernel of a Linear Transformation
decisions.reason: Outside expansion; first kernel vocabulary, basis and nullity of a transformation. Parent verified textbook5.7 explicitly requires kernels, kernel bases and trivial-kernel criterion.

evidence.detail: Ker(T)=Null(standard matrix).
Nullity(T)=dim Ker(T)=nullity(matrix).
Find basis of kernel from a 2x2 map.

decisions.downstream_benefit: Course kernel coverage; transfers null-space learning to transformation language.

decisions.topic_name: The Rank-Nullity Theorem in Terms of Linear Transformations
decisions.reason: Outside expansion; parent verified textbook5.7 explicitly requires dimension(V)=dimension(kernel)+dimension(image). Descriptions of image/kernel and bijection implications make transfer from the matrix theorem substantially easier.

evidence.detail: Rank/nullity of transformation with image y+2z=0.
Given independent image generators, infer standard-matrix rank/nullity/bijection.
Infer nullity from image defined by -x+z=0.

decisions.downstream_benefit: Rank-nullity in transformation language and image-dimension reasoning.

decisions.topic_name: Linear Combinations of Vectors in N-Dimensional Euclidean Space
decisions.reason: Genuinely useful elementary coefficient training, but current learned Span and Independence lessons already use exactly the same vector-to-system conversion and solve 2/3 coefficients. Eight direct practice mass on this unlearned topic further supports bypassing its whole lesson.

evidence.detail: Two coefficients from vector equality.
Three coefficients from 3D vectors.
One coefficient with R4 vectors.

decisions.downstream_benefit: Skills supplied by learned Span 48315 and Independence50426; no new dependency is introduced by skipping.

decisions.topic_name: Linear Combinations of Vectors and Their Properties
decisions.reason: Geometric head-to-tail combination drawing plus equating abstract coefficients for nonparallel vectors is not used by retained lessons; numerical linear combination meaning is already practiced in learned span/independence.

evidence.detail: Draw 2a+3b.
Solve alpha,beta by coefficient equality for a nonparallel pair.

decisions.downstream_benefit: No required retained downstream question uses diagram construction or this abstract coefficient trick.

decisions.topic_name: Subspaces of Abstract Vector Spaces
decisions.reason: Whole lesson is polynomial/matrix/function subspace classification, outside supplied Euclidean coursework. Basic+geometric subspace lessons already supply closure proofs and counterexamples; no retained question needs abstract vector axioms or polynomial/function ambient spaces.

evidence.detail: Polynomial subset at^3-bt.
Matrices with nonnegative trace: addition yes, negative scaling no.
Continuous functions satisfying f(0)=-f(2).
Constant continuous functions, select closure statements.

decisions.downstream_benefit: Retained lessons use R^n only; skip stops its continuity/axiom prerequisite branch.

decisions.topic_name: Defining Abstract Vector Spaces
decisions.reason: Formal axiom definition and completing axiom-labelled proofs are not used by any retained subspace/rank/image question. Closure criterion is directly taught in retained Euclidean lessons.

evidence.detail: Fill axiom labels in proof w+w=w implies w=0.
Degree exactly3 polynomials fail addition closure.

decisions.downstream_benefit: No formal axiomatic proof demand in actual guide2-4 or WHW4/5.

decisions.topic_name: Introduction to Abstract Vector Spaces
decisions.reason: Mostly abstract closure/property identification and eight-property tables for polynomials/functions/matrices. Useful for a later abstract-vector course, but no retained lesson needs those settings.

evidence.detail: Degree>=5 polynomials not closed under addition.
Identify matrix identity/commutativity statements.
Functions f(0)=1 fail closure.

decisions.downstream_benefit: Euclidean closure retained directly; no need to add polynomial/function/complex prerequisite chain.

decisions.topic_name: Continuity Over an Interval
decisions.reason: Continuity of graph intervals is only relevant to skipped abstract-function examples. Even those examples ask evaluation closure, not diagnosing discontinuities.

evidence.detail: Identify open intervals of continuity from a graph.
Identify largest continuity intervals.

decisions.downstream_benefit: No retained downstream question uses continuity or endpoint analysis.

decisions.topic_name: Describing Planar Regions Using Set-Builder Notation
decisions.reason: Whole lesson trains describing shaded planar sets, with boundary inclusion. Retained subspace lesson explicitly introduces its needed set-builder reading, and geometric sequel asks membership/closure rather than authoring regions.

evidence.detail: Write rectangle inequalities with open/closed edges.
Describe parabolic shaded region in set-builder notation.

decisions.downstream_benefit: Guide bounded slab notation and retained set conditions require reading a condition only; supplied by basic subspace tutorial.

decisions.topic_name: The Cartesian Equation of a Plane
decisions.reason: Whole normal-vector/cross-product Cartesian plane construction is not used by retained subspace questions; those give an equation or derive simple parameterized coordinates inside the lesson.

evidence.detail: Find Cartesian plane through point perpendicular to normal.
Find plane parallel to two vectors using normal.

decisions.downstream_benefit: Retained Subspaces51046 checks a supplied plane equation; no need for normal-vector construction.

decisions.topic_name: The Vector Equation of a Plane
decisions.reason: Dot-product normal form of a plane and finding parallel vectors/perpendicular-line planes do not appear in retained subspace questions. Learned Parametric Plane50308 supplies the representation actually used.

evidence.detail: Find plane perpendicular to a parametric line.
Find missing components in a vector parallel to plane.

decisions.downstream_benefit: WHW5 w dot u=0 uses closure/linearity, not constructing a normal-form plane.

decisions.topic_name: The Cartesian Equation of a Line
decisions.reason: Retained basic subspace lesson derives its own simple Cartesian ratio from a direction vector. Full Cartesian-line lesson adds zero-denominator cases and equation conversions not asked downstream.

evidence.detail: Convert given parametric line to Cartesian ratios.
Handle zero direction component.

decisions.downstream_benefit: Studied Vector Equation Line49485 (practice accuracy~1.00,mass21.25) and retained subspace derivation suffice.

decisions.topic_name: The Parametric Equations of a Line
decisions.reason: Parametric/vector conversion and line segments are supplied where needed by learned vector-line and parametric-plane work; no retained question asks restricted line segments.

evidence.detail: Rewrite parametric equations as vector equation.
Parametrize a bounded line segment.

decisions.downstream_benefit: Retained subspace lessons use unrestricted real parameters and derive coordinate form themselves.

decisions.topic_name: Solving 2x2 Systems of Equations Using Inverse Matrices
decisions.reason: The IMT2x2 whole lesson asks implications and determinant recognition, not solving by A inverse b. Learned Inverses2x2 and MatrixColumnVector already supply inverse/product meanings and computations if needed.

evidence.detail: Solve system specifically using inverse matrix.
Inverse method unavailable when determinant0.

decisions.downstream_benefit: No retained IMT question requires performing inverse solution; learned inverse accuracy .923,mass14.33 and product accuracy~1,mass21.

decisions.topic_name: The Four Fundamental Subspaces of a Matrix
decisions.reason: Does define row space, but entire lesson adds orthogonal complements, four-space dimension identities and their images; does not teach row-basis extraction. Poor whole-lesson bridge for WHW5 final problem. Flag narrow row-space/row-operation transfer rather than asserting this topic repairs it.

evidence.detail: Row space=Col(A^T); left nullspace and orthogonal complements.
Image of row space under A is Col(A).
Orthogonal subspace of Null(XY) requires transpose product.
Dimension of Col from left-null dimension.

decisions.downstream_benefit: Can compute a valid row basis by applying retained BasisSpan to original rows (transpose); row-space definition and reduced-nonzero-row rule still need course transfer evidence.

decisions.topic_name: The Invertible Matrix Theorem in Terms of Linear Transformations
decisions.reason: Outside119 and a real prerequisite of the whole retained transformation rank-nullity lesson: its mixed bank assumes bijection/invertibility. The whole lesson is materially useful, beyond notation translation, because collision and missing-image premises require connecting transformations to nontrivial kernel and deficient rank. Learned Invertible Functions49731 supplies general inverse-function meaning but not these linear consequences.

evidence.detail: Defines inverse linear transformation/bijection, states invertible iff standard matrix invertible, translates Col/Null/rank/nullity to image/kernel.
T(v1)=T(v2) with distinct vectors implies nonzero v1-v2 in kernel and rank<8.
Same collision argument tested in R7; rejects invertibility/full rank.
A vector outside image forces deficient rank and nontrivial kernel in the square setting.

decisions.downstream_benefit: Makes rank-nullity transformation mixed practice and textbook5.3 inverse-map/matrix equivalence accessible; concrete model for one-to-one/kernel argument.
decisions.limitation: Square Rn->Rn only; cannot replace required general textbook5.7 proof for subspaces V,W or justify one-to-one iff onto for rectangular maps.

scope_note: Parent verified textbook5.7 kernel/image subspace proofs, basis for each, trivial-kernel criterion and transformation rank-nullity; in-class completeness remains parent audit. Guide explicitly names WHW4/5 and chapters4.10.4,4.10.5,5.1-5.4,5.7; guide2-4 alone are not exhaustive.

transfer_gaps.detail: Retained subspace lessons show symbolic closure and image lesson gives witnesses, but practice asks classification/numerical preimages. Student must choose preimages u=Ax,v=Ay and use A(x+y),A(cx),A0; no captured lesson asks constructing this proof.

Coordinates teaches arbitrary basis expansion; ImageRank proves/uses standard matrix column-space equality only. Need both inclusions using x=sum c_i v_i, linearity, and converse sum c_i T(v_i)=T(sum c_i v_i). Parent set-proof audit covers inclusion technique.
Geometric disk/half-plane counterexamples teach the move but practice is classification. Need explicit member (4,0,0,0) and scalar2 to disprove scalar closure.

transfer_gaps.task: Textbook5.7 kernel/image subspace and basis proofs
transfer_gaps.detail: Kernel49903 proves T(0)=0 and identifies Ker(T)=Null(matrix), but its questions are numerical membership, basis or nullity. No retained question asks arbitrary u,v in Ker(T) then T(alpha u+beta v)=0. ImageRank similarly lacks symbolic image closure. BasisSpan/ColumnBasis/NullBasis provide computations; learner must connect a spanning image set or null parameterization to proof of independent spanning.

transfer_gaps.task: Rank-nullity on V a subspace, and one-to-one criterion
transfer_gaps.detail: TransformationRankNullity49880 states its theorem for T:R^n->R^n and uses n as domain dimension; its mixed practice also assumes bijection/invertibility vocabulary. Actual textbook5.7 needs dimension(V) for an arbitrary subspace domain, including non-square maps. Parent transformation branch must cover trivial-kernel iff one-to-one, and the basis argument for dimension(V)=dimensionKer+dimensionImage; retained numerical rank-nullity lessons alone do not prove it.

transfer_gaps.severity: coverage gap unless coursework supplies it
transfer_gaps.detail: Retained BasisSpan can be applied to transposed rows to yield a valid original-row basis. None of kept lessons explicitly names row space or proves elementary row operations preserve it / nonzero echelon rows form its basis. FourFundamental defines row space but does not teach extraction and brings unrelated orthogonal-complement machinery. Parent should identify existing coursework treatment; do not silently claim no gap.

Retained dimension, nullity, IMT teach needed pivot facts. Their practice remains numerical/statement classification, so learner must write independent columns -> no free variables -> full square rank -> every RHS attainable, and m x (m+1) -> free variable -> nontrivial relation.

textbook57_note: Parent verified V,W are subspaces of Rn; abstract polynomial/function/matrix domains are unnecessary. Kernel49903 and transformationRankNullity49880 are firm keeps. Parent must cover one-to-one/trivial-kernel theorem with transformation branch.

content_caveats.detail: Tutorial17592186121057 labels zero-space basis as no basis; mathematically empty set is its basis. Retained NullBasis48823 and IMT practice17592186125167 correctly explain empty basis. Do not repeat the tutorial error.
First criterion omits explicit nonempty condition; all practiced lines/planes are nonempty. Written general subspace tests must establish zero membership/nonemptiness (image via A0).

final_independent_challenge.decision_context: Final independent challenge of general proof bridge and function-set foundation; whole lessons only.

evidence: Tutorial17592186173160 uses missing arrows and a changed domain to distinguish range from codomain.
Example17592186171840 and practice17592186645038 distinguish the stated target set from actual range; the learned introductory transformation topic does not supply this distinction.
sets_and_functions.order: Before Image and Rank, kernel/range and one-to-one/onto course work.

proof_bridge.content_value: Witness rewriting in tutorials17592186205271/17592186205278 and two inclusions in17592186205285/example17592186203728 are directly transferable to guide4. This is the better conceptual proof bridge of the two inspected topics.
proof_bridge.whole_lesson_cost: Includes modular conditional definitions and trigonometric subset/equality problems alongside the useful integer witnesses. Full practice bank is8questions and18select fields; all fields have null correctAnswer and every solution is empty. available=true merely indicates lesson content accessible, not a verified complete assessment.
proof_bridge.practice_limit: Captured practice asks starting sets, counterexample target or inclusion headings, not carrying out the actual witness rewriting or two-inclusion proof. Repairing answer keys alone would still not make it proof-production assessment.
proof_bridge.recommendation: Do not add an incomplete broad proof lesson as a mandatory near-exam prerequisite. Keep required original guide2–4 and textbook5.7 written proof practice as part of completion; these are original required coursework, not partial-study slices or newly authored lessons. This decision does not assert proof mastery.
proof_bridge.counterfactual: For a separate proof-writing curriculum, this whole lesson is a reasonable candidate after completing its assessment and checking modular/trig readiness; that is outside the present read-only audit.
